api:
<BlandAltman data={readings} a={|r: &Reading| r.cuff} b={|r: &Reading| r.arterial} a_label="Cuff" b_label="Arterial line" />
PropTypeDefault
dataas aboverequired
a, bFn(&T) -> f64: the same quantity by two methodsrequired
a_label, b_labeltext, used in the axis titles"A", "B"
agreementf64: the width of the limits of agreement, in standard deviations1.96 (95%)
colorcolour of the pointsthe first series colour
legend, tooltip, classas on <XYChart>

Each point is the mean of the two methods (x) against their difference, a − b (y). Lines mark the bias (the mean difference) and bias ± agreement × SD.

Zoom: drag a rectangle to zoom into it, Ctrl and scroll to zoom about the pointer, and double-click to reset.

examples.title: Two methods
examples.description: Difference against mean, with the bias and 95% limits of agreement.
examples.code:
#[component]
fn pressure() {
    let data = use_signal(readings(1));
    rsx! { <BlandAltman data={data} a={|r: &Reading| r.cuff} b={|r: &Reading| r.arterial} a_label="Cuff" b_label="Arterial line" class="h-72" /> }
}

examples.title: 99% limits
examples.code:
#[component]
fn ninety_five() {
    let data = use_signal(readings(2));
    rsx! { <BlandAltman data={data} a={|r: &Reading| r.cuff} b={|r: &Reading| r.arterial} agreement={2.58} color={rgb(0x179299)} class="h-72" /> }
}

examples.title: Proportional bias
examples.description: One method reads 8% high: the differences grow with the mean.
examples.code:
#[component]
fn biased() {
    let data = use_signal(
        readings(3)
            .into_iter()
            .map(|reading| Reading {
                cuff: reading.cuff * 1.08,
                ..reading
            })
            .collect::<Vec<_>>(),
    );
    rsx! { <BlandAltman data={data} a={|r: &Reading| r.cuff} b={|r: &Reading| r.arterial} class="h-72" /> }
}

examples.title: No legend or tooltip
examples.description: Only the points and the three lines.
examples.code:
#[component]
fn bare() {

    rsx! { <BlandAltman data={data} a={|r: &Reading| r.cuff} b={|r: &Reading| r.arterial} legend={Legend::hidden()} tooltip={Tooltip::hidden()} class="h-72" /> }
}

examples.title: ±1 SD limits
examples.description: agreement 1 narrows the limits to about 68%.
examples.code:
#[component]
fn one_sigma() {
    let data = use_signal(readings(5));
    rsx! { <BlandAltman data={data} a={|r: &Reading| r.cuff} b={|r: &Reading| r.arterial} agreement={1.} color={rgb(0x8839ef)} class="h-72" /> }
}

examples.title: Constant offset
examples.description: The cuff reads 10 mmHg high everywhere, so the bias line sits above zero.
examples.code:
#[component]
fn constant_offset() {
    let data = use_signal(adjusted(6, 1., 10.));
    rsx! { <BlandAltman data={data} a={|r: &Reading| r.cuff} b={|r: &Reading| r.arterial} a_label="Cuff" b_label="Arterial line" class="h-72" /> }
}

examples.title: Under-reading

examples.title: 3 SD limits
examples.description: A very conservative band of agreement.
examples.code:
#[component]
fn wide_agreement() {
    let data = use_signal(adjusted(8, 1., -4.));
    rsx! { <BlandAltman data={data} a={|r: &Reading| r.cuff} b={|r: &Reading| r.arterial} agreement={3.} color={rgb(0x179299)} class="h-72" /> }

examples.title: Methods swapped
examples.description: Swapping a and b flips the sign of the differences.
examples.code:
#[component]
fn swapped() {
    let data = use_signal(readings(9));
    rsx! { <BlandAltman data={data} a={|r: &Reading| r.arterial} b={|r: &Reading| r.cuff} a_label="Arterial line" b_label="Cuff" class="h-72" /> }
}

examples.title: One-sided 95%
examples.description: A small bias and 1.645 SD limits for a one-sided check.
examples.code:
#[component]
fn well_matched() {
    let data = use_signal(adjusted(10, 1., -3.));
    rsx! { <BlandAltman data={data} a={|r: &Reading| r.cuff} b={|r: &Reading| r.arterial} a_label="Oscillometric" b_label="Invasive" agreement={1.645} color={rgb(0x40a02b)} class="h-72" /> }
}
